cohort: 1291 pregnant women with COVID-19, of whom 59 delivered while infected, in Mie Prefecture, Japan, from December 2020 to August 2022
finding: The number of caesarean sections performed without medical indication and the rate of neonatal complications associated with caesarean section increased during the COVID-19 pandemic.
mod_finding: Neonatal complications were significantly more common with caesarean section than with vaginal delivery, and there were no cases of COVID-19 infection in healthcare workers.
